question.text: Vertical displacement of a plank with a body of mass \(m\) on it is varying according to law \(y=\sin \omega t+\sqrt{3} \cos \omega t\). The minimum value of \(\omega\) for which the mass just breaks off the plank and the moment it occurs first after \(\mathrm{t}=0\), are given by

solution.text:
From, figure, $$ \begin{array}{ll} & \Lambda_{\mathrm{R}}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^{2}+(1)^{2}}-2 \\ & \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3} \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{y}=2 \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \end{array} $$
$$ \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=\mathrm{a}=-2 \omega^{2} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) $$ $a_{\max }=-2 \omega^{2}=g$ For which mass just breaks off the plank $\omega=\sqrt{\mathrm{g} / 2}$ This will be happen for the first time when $$ \begin{array}{l} \omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{2} \text { or } \omega \mathrm{t}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{t}=\frac{\pi}{6 \omega}=\frac{\pi}{6} \sqrt{\frac{2}{\mathrm{~g}}} \end{array} $$
